subject: CloudBridge marketplace: residency & retention acceptance criteria Q&A
messages:
From: Sam Patel <sam.patel@cloudbridge.io>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>
Cc: partners@cloudbridge.io
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 16:09:00 -0700
Subject: Marketplace listing - residency / retention questions

Hi Aisha,

Thanks for the intro earlier this week. As we move toward the CloudBridge listing for Redwood in the marketplace, procurement and security have a few acceptance items we need clarified so we can finalize the commercial. Can you confirm the following across AWS / GCP / Azure? I've attached our baseline doc (CB-Residency-Reqs-v2.pdf).

Top questions:
- Can Redwood guarantee tenant-level region lock? Example: customers who commit to us-west-2 must have their model inference, logs, and backups confined to that region.
- What are the default retention windows for logs, model cache, and customer artifacts? Can these be shortened on request (DSRs)?
- Deletion SLA: if a customer requests deletion, how long until data + backups + KV cache are fully removed? Is there a documented playbook for the marketplace?
- KMS / CMEK options: do you support customer-managed keys in each cloud marketplace flow?
- Snapshots / cross-region replication: are there scenarios where Redwood will replicate snapshots cross-region for durability? If so, is that opt-in?

We need concise answers to include in our security review. If you prefer, we can take a short alignment call next week.

Best,
Sam
Head of Partnerships | CloudBridge

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Marketplace listing - residency / retention questions

Hi Sam —

Thanks for the clear list and the attachment. High level answers below; I've also attached a condensed Redwood residency matrix (redwood-residency-matrix.xlsx) that maps capabilities by cloud and common region names. Happy to jump on a 30m call to walk through specifics.

Quick answers (AWS / GCP / Azure):
- Tenant-level region lock: supported via routing + pinned deployment. We can pin a tenant to a specific region and prevent fallbacks to other regions for inference and logging. This applies to hosted & marketplace flows when customers select a region at onboarding.
- Retention defaults: logs = 90 days (configurable 7–365), model KV cache = ephemeral (default cleared after 24 hrs of inactivity; can be persisted for warm-starts with explicit agreement), customer artifacts (uploads) = 90 days default; retention windows are configurable per-tenant via the console or API.
- Deletion SLA: documented playbook is our standard — deletion requests trigger immediate logical deletion, background purge of backups/snapshots within 30 days, and final verification + audit log entry within 45 days. We can offer accelerated purge (14 days) for marketplace enterprise deals under contract.
- KMS / CMEK: supported in all three clouds for Private and Dedicated customers. For marketplace-hosted listings, CMEK is available for customers who provision a key and provide access; Redwood can integrate with partner-managed KMS via marketplace-approved flows.
- Cross-region replication: disabled by default for tenant-pinned deployments. For redundancy we offer replication only if explicitly enabled; we document cross-region replicas and require customer opt-in and contractual notice.

Action items for CloudBridge procurement:
1) Confirm which clouds / exact regions CloudBridge wants listed as allowed by default for the customer onboarding flow (e.g., AWS: us-west-2; GCP: us-central1; Azure: eastus2).
2) If accelerated deletion (14-day) is required, we will surface that as a commercial add-on.
3) If CMEK will be required for every listing, we'll need to align on key-provisioning steps and an integration test.

CC'ing Neha for compliance + audit details, and Karthik to track acceptance criteria on the Marketplace checklist.

Thanks,
Aisha Rahman
Senior Partner Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Hi Sam — quick compliance addendum from our side. Below are the acceptance criteria we typically include in Marketplace SOWs. These are intentionally concise so procurement has a checklist to sign off on.

Redwood proposed acceptance checklist (for CloudBridge listing):
- Region lock: Tenant-level pinning confirmed; routing policies and fallbacks documented in the listing. No automatic cross-region fallback for pinned tenants.
- Data types covered: inference payloads, model KV cache, logs, customer uploads, audit logs, backups/snapshots.
- Retention policy: default 90d logs, configurable; retention updates honored within 24 hours in configs, changes applied to new data; legacy archives purged per deletion SLA.
- Deletion & purge: Logical deletion immediate; physical purge of backups/snapshots within 30 days by default. Contractual accelerated purge = 14 days with additional verification and a one-time fee if KMS rekeying is required.
- Backup handling: backups inherit tenant region unless opt-in cross-region replication requested; replication requires explicit opt-in and documented justification.
- KMS/CMEK: customer-managed keys supported for encryption-at-rest; key access patterns and rotation documented; if CMEK is used, snapshot export requires KMS policy that allows Redwood's service principal read/decrypt rights limited to the minimum scope.
- Auditability: deletion and retention changes create immutable audit events; we provide an exportable audit CSV for SOC2 evidence.
- Evidence for security review: SOC2 Type II report, config snapshot demonstrating tenant pinning, and a deletion playbook (we can provide sample artifacts).

Notes / clarifying points:
- Marketplace flows: some cloud marketplaces have limitations on key handover; if CloudBridge is listing as the transactor, we will run a marketplace-specific key-provisioning test during onboarding.
- Edge cases: emergency support may require short-term cross-region access for incident response; this is logged and requires approvals per our incident access policy.

If CloudBridge wants, I can provide the SOC2 export and a short sample audit CSV.

Neha Kapoor
Compliance & Security Programs | Redwood Inference
